_comment: Ordered cascade of external AI endpoints. The Lambda tries each enabled endpoint in order; the first that answers wins. Groq is ALWAYS appended as the final fallback in code. 'secret' is the AWS Secrets Manager id. 'kind' selects the call method.
_incident_2026_08_17: Groq decommissioned llama-3.3-70b-versatile and llama-3.1-8b-instant (announced 17 Jun, effective Aug 2026) and EVERY service went down at once. The cascade looked redundant and was not: three entries, one vendor, two models, both on the same deprecation notice — three doors into the same room. The lesson is that redundancy means a second PROVIDER, not a second model. ovh-gpt-oss-120b below is that second provider: EU-hosted (Gravelines), serving the same open-weight model, so a Groq decision can no longer take the product offline. Enabled 21 Sep 2026, paid and uncapped, which also ends the free-tier daily-quota cliff.

endpoints.name: ovh-gpt-oss-120b
endpoints._note: The second PROVIDER the August incident called for: EU-hosted (Gravelines), paid and uncapped, serving the same open-weight model — so neither a Groq outage nor a spent daily quota can take the product offline. Host and model string verified against the OVH AI Endpoints catalogue on 21 Sep 2026; EUR 0.08/0.40 per million tokens in/out. Deliberately placed AFTER Groq: this is the safety net, and voice keeps the fastest provider until this one's time-to-first-token has been benchmarked. Open item for the DPIA: OVH documents Gravelines + zero retention, but written confirmation that AI Endpoints processing is EU-only is still outstanding.

endpoints.name: groq-gpt-oss-20b
endpoints._note: Smaller and faster; last Groq resort before the in-code fallback.
